answers: acceptance-gate finding 1: not mine — the finding reports that test files do not carry SPEC tag annotations (e.g. `[DSPRB-1]`). Placing those tags in test files is the test-author's output, not the design's. My design defines every SPEC with its id, Given/When/Then contract, and `covers:` mapping precisely so the test-author can produce correctly-tagged assertions. The design cannot and must not write test files; that is the test-author stage's job.

acceptance-gate finding 2: not mine — the WIRING check failing for `scripts/lib/compat.sh` and `scripts/lib/helpers.sh` is a downstream consequence of the test-author not yet having created tagged test files; without a test tagged to those files, the pipeline has nothing to run when it reverts them. `WIRING: none` is correct on its own terms: the probe variables are set and consumed entirely within the library files being modified; no external file calls the new probe behavior directly; external callers reach `zbuild_sed_inplace` and `_zb_target_mode_v` through unchanged function names. The declaration is accurate and requires no change.
